question: What is the primary structural target of the immune system attack in disseminated sclerosis?
explanation: The pathology of disseminated sclerosis centers on the autoimmune destruction of myelin within the central nervous system. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h1)

question: How does demyelination directly affect nerve impulse transmission?

options.A: It slows or completely blocks electrical signal conduction
options.B: It permanently converts sensory neurons into motor neurons
options.C: It accelerates the speed of neurotransmitter release
options.D: It increases the production of cerebrospinal fluid

explanation: Without the insulating properties of the myelin sheath, electrical impulses cannot travel efficiently along the axon, leading to disrupted neurological function. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which environmental viral infection is frequently linked as a trigger for disseminated sclerosis?
explanation: Epidemiological studies consistently show a strong association between past Epstein-Barr virus infection and subsequent development of demyelinating disease. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h2)

question: Why has the recognition of disseminated sclerosis shifted within clinical practice in regions like Nigeria?

options.A: A sudden mutation making the virus exclusively tropical
options.B: Improved diagnostic imaging and heightened clinical awareness
options.C: Mandatory genetic screening at birth for all infants
options.D: The complete eradication of all other neurological disorders

explanation: Better access to neurodiagnostics and specialized training have reduced underdiagnosis in areas previously thought to be completely free of the condition. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h2)

question: Which visual symptom is frequently one of the earliest presenting signs of disseminated sclerosis?
explanation: Inflammation of the optic nerve often causes sudden blurring and pain with eye movement, serving as a classic early indicator of the disease. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h3)

question: A patient describes unpredictable episodes of acute neurological worsening lasting a few weeks, separated by months of complete baseline recovery. Which disease pattern matches this description?
explanation: The relapsing-remitting pattern features distinct attacks of symptoms followed by periods of remission without disease progression between episodes. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is considered the gold standard imaging modality for identifying central nervous system plaques in disseminated sclerosis?
explanation: Magnetic resonance imaging provides superior soft-tissue contrast required to visualize characteristic demyelinating lesions in the brain and spinal cord. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h4)

question: What specific cerebrospinal fluid finding strongly supports a diagnosis of disseminated sclerosis during a lumbar puncture?

options.D: Complete absence of white blood cells

explanation: Oligoclonal bands represent localized antibody production within the central nervous system, which is a hallmark feature of autoimmune demyelination. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary pharmacological objective of administering high-dose corticosteroids during an acute relapse?

options.A: To permanently regenerate destroyed myelin sheaths
options.B: To cure the underlying autoimmune genetic defect
options.C: To permanently eliminate all future relapse events
options.D: To suppress inflammation and shorten attack duration

explanation: Corticosteroids act as potent anti-inflammatory agents that reduce the severity and length of acute neurological flare-ups. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of disease-modifying therapies in the long-term management of disseminated sclerosis?

options.A: To replace lost cerebrospinal fluid volume
options.C: To immediately reverse existing neurological scars
options.D: To reduce relapse frequency and delay disability progression

explanation: Disease-modifying therapies modulate the immune system to decrease overall disease activity and slow the accumulation of permanent physical disability. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why is energy conservation and activity pacing a central component of daily nursing care for these patients?

options.A: Chronic fatigue is a pervasive and debilitating symptom of the disease
options.B: Lethal exhaustion can occur from minor movements
options.C: Physical activity instantly destroys remaining myelin sheaths
options.D: Muscles atrophy within hours if not kept strictly resting

explanation: Fatigue in disseminated sclerosis is often overwhelming and distinct from normal tiredness, requiring structured pacing strategies to maintain function. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h6)

question: Which nursing intervention is most appropriate for a patient experiencing neurogenic bladder dysfunction with urinary retention?

options.A: Encouraging prolonged breath-holding to stimulate urination
options.B: Restricting all fluid intake to less than 200 milliliters daily
options.C: Instructing on clean intermittent self-catheterization techniques
options.D: Applying high-pressure abdominal massage every hour

explanation: Intermittent catheterization safely empties the bladder, reduces residual urine volume, and prevents urinary tract infections associated with neurogenic retention. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h6)

question: Which professional discipline focuses specifically on helping patients adapt daily living activities and utilize adaptive home equipment?
explanation: Occupational therapists evaluate home environments and recommend adaptive tools to help patients maintain independence in self-care and daily routines. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h7)

question: What is a critical risk in the advanced stages of progressive disseminated sclerosis that requires careful pulmonary monitoring?
explanation: As neurological degeneration advances, weakness in the intercostal muscles and diaphragm can compromise adequate ventilation and airway clearance. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h7)
